newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's investment in China drops in Jan-June.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's investment in China drops in Jan-June.

text.p: Taiwan's investment in rival China slid 10.93 percent between January and June this year from the same period a year ago after Taipei adopted a tough investment policy towards Beijing, the Investment Commission said on Sunday.
The commission approved 243 indirect China investment projects worth US$495.789 million by Taiwan companies in the first six months of 1997, down 10.93 percent from 1996.
In June alone, Taiwan approved 57 mainland investment projects worth $105.512 million.
Jiangsu, Guangdong, Fujian, Shandong, and Sichuan provinces were the most favourite destinations for Taiwan investors. Together they accounted for 89 percent of Taiwan firms' total investment there.

Electronic and electric manufacturing industries topped the list of Taiwan companies' investment in China, followed by basic metal and metal manufacturing, food and drinks manufacturing, transportation tools, and the chemical manufacturing industries.

Worried that the island may become over-dependent on the mainland for investment, President Lee Teng-hui said in August 1996 that the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market.
Taiwan's overseas investment, excluding that in mainland China, rose 16.62 percent between January and June to $1.260 billion from the same period in 1996.
The government has urged local companies to "refrain from temptation" and put national interest before their own when considering investing in the mainland.

Taiwanese officials, including Lee Teng-hui, have repeatedly accused China of using commerce as a political lever against the island, and told local businessmen it was time to slow their investment projects in the mainland.

Though all investments in China must be government approved and routed indirectly through Hong Kong or other third places, Taiwan remains concerned that its economy may become too dependent on China -- and hence politically vulnerable.
Taiwan has banned all direct official contact with China since a civil war split the two sides in 1949.
Despite the ban, indirect commerce has flourished since the late 1980s when political tensions started to thaw. Some 30,000 Taiwan companies have poured more than US$30 billion into China so far.
